author: reek
body: It is not a replacement for GopBoot and does not duplicate it. The ceremony writes the identity this stick carries and the menu is how a person chooses an interface; both stay where they are. This is the instrument, and it is built the way the run sheet asks every rung to be built: it answers one question and it cannot be held up by another.

author: reek
body: The same shape as GopBoot's boot-trace and for the same reason: on real metal there is no serial port, so the boot narrates itself on the glass and the last line standing names the stage that died.

author: reek
body: Four bars in a fixed order and the mode the payload believes it is painting into. A stride or mode mismatch shows as banded smear rather than clean bars, and the order red, green, blue, white exposes a BGR/RGB swap at a glance.

author: reek
body: The fuel is the floor for a machine whose RTC never advances, which is the one case a clock cannot measure. It is spent per iteration rather than per second, so it bounds the hold on a dead clock without ever shortening it on a live one.

author: reek
body: Ten seconds, and the window says how much of itself is left. The hold runs BEFORE runtime-init, so there is no IDT, no IRQ and no key cell yet: nothing can shorten it and nothing can extend it, which makes the printed number the only thing the operator has to work with.

author: reek
body: Ten seconds with the table and the live counters on the glass, and any key ends the hold at once. A working keyboard therefore costs one tap and proves delivery before the desktop paints; a dead one leaves ten seconds to photograph the table and a counters row updating every second, which together name every bound interface and say which of them, if any, ever carried a non-zero report.

author: reek
body: The first flight of this hold never showed its table: the boot-menu Enter was still releasing when the hold's first poll ran, so a pending scancode skipped it inside one frame. Two guards now: the mailbox is drained once before the hold starts, and a key ends the hold only after the dwell -- the first three seconds are a floor, so the table is on the glass long enough to photograph whatever is pre-loaded.

author: reek
body: runtime-init installs the GDT, IDT, TSS, syscall MSRs and the PIC/PIT and keyboard setup; usb-attach enumerates the bus once, configuring every keyboard interface and the boot stick on the same running controllers; medium-select locks GopDisk onto the disk carrying our own CODEX.CDX so a real machine's internal drive cannot shadow the boot stick. Then the desktop, and the desktop is where this payload stops. There is nothing behind it to return to.
